name: Casper Mountain County Park - Skunk Hollow Campground
note: Natrona County campground on Casper Mountain, with sites spread along the gated, one-way gravel Strube Loop under pines and aspens, among granite climbing boulders and bike trails; each site has a fire ring and picnic table. The county publishes no site lengths, so confirm with the Parks Department that a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Natrona County Parks Rec1 catalog (secure.rec1.com/WY/natrona-county-wy/catalog, public getTabs/getItems/getLocationFacilities JSON, tab 12056 'Casper Mountain', group 24913 'Skunk Hollow', read 2026-11-20): 'Closed for winter. Reopens 5/28/2027. Reservation Only. Available 90 days in advance. The Skunk Hollow Campgrounds are located on Strube Loop on Casper Mountain ... Skunk Hollow has 10 sites. Each campsite has a fire ring and a picnic table. $13.39 a night plus taxes and fees'; 10 bookable items SH Site 01-10 at a 2026 'Nightly Rate' of $13.39. Rec1 group photos: entrance sign 'SKUNK HOLLOW CAMPGROUND / CAMPING PERMIT REQUIRED' beside a 'ONE WAY' sign on a graded gravel road; SH 3's photo shows a dirt pull-in with picnic table. Google Maps 'Elkhorn Springs Campground' (4.4 on 66 reviews; Google has no separate Skunk Hollow place) carries a ~2025 review 'Stayed at skunk hollow. Site 6 was awesome'. Mountain Project (Skunk Hollow climbing area, read 2026-11-20): 'Drive on Strube Loop ... park at any of the numerous campsites'. County silent on rig length and no source shows pads under ~23 ft or tent-only/walk-in sites -> kept with an unclear-fit caveat (AWH 2026-11-02 unclear-pad rule); no agency road warning found (county pages 403, unread). Public (local): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery frames rendered at 42.74109,-106.31966 (~350 m half-width), 42.7400,-106.3175 (~800 m), 42.7410,-106.3200 and 42.7425,-106.3160 (~220 m) and 42.7400,-106.3150 (~160 m): Strube Loop is a gravel road through dense pine/aspen forest, with a narrow grassy drainage (Elkhorn Creek headwater, no open water visible) along its east limb and small dirt pull-offs beside the road there; no lake, pond or river anywhere in the 1.6 km frame. A ~2025 Google reviewer wrote that Skunk Hollow 'Site 6 ... had a creek running through it' - a review, not a site-level basis, and the site cannot be placed on the stream under the canopy. Default down -> not waterfront (creekside would need a site-level source, as for 15734 Elkhorn Springs).

facilities.note: One restroom, some sites a walk from it; no water at any Casper Mountain campground.

facilities_source: Rec1 tab 12056 ('Restroom facilities are provided at each Casper Mountain Campground. Water is not available at any of the Casper Mountain Campgrounds.') + campgroundviews.com ('A single restroom is available for campers; however, some campsites may be a distance from this facility.'), read 2026-11-20. Toilet type (vault/flush) not stated anywhere read.

season.note: Reopens May 28, 2027; the county does not publish a closing date.

season_source: Rec1 group 24913 ('Closed for winter. Reopens 5/28/2027.'), read 2026-11-20.

booking.note: Reservation only, online (Rec1) or through the county Parks Department.

booking_source: Rec1 group 24913 ('Reservation Only. Available 90 days in advance.') + tab 12056 ('Casper Mountain Campgrounds are by reservation only'); Rec1 site photos (SH Site 01-10, EXIF Sep-Nov 2022) show each site's sign 'SH n / 10 DAY CAMPING LIMIT / ENJOY YOUR STAY / RESERVATIONS REQUIRED', read 2026-11-20.
flags: Rig fit unverified: the county publishes no site lengths; its campground map (natronacounty-wy.gov DocumentCenter/View/6376/SkunkHollowElkhornSprings_041321, linked from the Rec1 group) was not fetched (site refuses). Rec1 photos show only site-number signs (SH 3: a dirt pull-in with table) and a graded one-way gravel entrance road; no review names a rig at Skunk Hollow. Kept with a caveat under the AWH 2026-11-02 unclear-pad rule; the reviewer may prefer to hold it.

Pin is the county's own 'Directions to Skunk Hollow' point (goo.gl -> Google's 'Strube Loop' road place, 42.74109,-106.31966), which sits on the loop's west limb; individual sites are not visible under the canopy. Mountain Project puts 'numerous campsites' along Strube Loop down to its NE bend (~42.7434,-106.3153, the Braille Trail parking), and the east limb shows dirt pull-offs around 42.7405,-106.3153. Whether those east-limb pull-offs are Skunk Hollow's or Elkhorn Springs' is unsettled without the county map.

~0.4 km NW of 15734 Elkhorn Springs (same Strube Loop area, shared county map PDF) but a separately named Rec1 facility with its own 10 sites (SH 01-10), so its own entry, not a duplicate. campgroundviews.com gives Skunk Hollow's GPS as 42.7382,-106.3166, essentially 15734's pin at the Casper Mountain Road junction - probably the shared entrance; Google resolves 'Skunk Hollow Campground' to the Elkhorn Springs place.
A ~2025 Google review says Skunk Hollow site 6 'had a creek running through it'; held at not waterfront for want of a site-level source (same call as 15734).
No Rec1 deep link for the group: the catalog's group URLs carry a hash not exposed in the JSON, so website/booking.url give the catalog root (as 15733 Deer Haven does).
